title: Inverse mates preserve square pasting
statement: Given three adjunctions E_i left adjoint to R_i, two successive pairs of functors F,G and F-prime,G-prime, composite functors H,H-prime, squares qf,qg,qh and comparison maps c,c-prime satisfying the restriction-square composition equation, their inverse mates satisfy the corresponding extension-square composition equation.

source.place: unit_mateEquiv_symm and the adjunction hom equivalence

proof.text: Transpose both sides under the last adjunction and use injectivity of its hom equivalence. Use unit_mateEquiv_symm for each square, naturality of the units and squares, and the assumed restriction-square composition equation. Both transposes coincide.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3), Remark 6.8.15; explicit formal coefficient and adjunction argument
proof_origin.note: B2: flat-resolution computation, exact derived-square transport, and proved inverse-mate pasting.

theorem inverseMate_pasting
    (hq : ∀ N : B₀,
      c.app (R₀.obj N) ≫ G.map (qf.app N) ≫ qg.app (F'.obj N) =
        qh.app N ≫ R₂.map (c'.app N)) (K : A₀) :
    E₂.map (c.app K) ≫
        ((mateEquiv a₁ a₂).symm (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ qg)).natTrans.app (F.obj K) ≫
        G'.map (((mateEquiv a₀ a₁).symm (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ qf)).natTrans.app K) =
      ((mateEquiv a₀ a₂).symm (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ qh)).natTrans.app K ≫
        c'.app (E₀.obj K)
